params.body:
The record I added this evening made the trends projection time out, and took the showcase graph and the taxonomy down with it.

**What it cost.** `recurrenceFor` read the corpus-wide monthly intake, its denominator, once per trend: a scan of 188,000 signals, 160ms each, 110 times. The projection went from a couple of seconds to eighteen, and the site gives up at ten. Measured against a copy of the live database: 14,259ms per-card, 1,979ms with the denominator read once.

**Why the other two endpoints failed as well.** The server is single threaded, so eighteen seconds of synchronous SQLite blocks everything queued behind it. They were not broken; they were waiting. Fixing the one fixes all three, which is worth knowing before anyone goes looking at the taxonomy.

`monthlyIntake(db)` is now the round's read and travels in as `shared`, along with `watchingSince`, which was a second scan for a value that cannot change between two trends measured a millisecond apart. A single trend still works on its own: the helper computes what it was not given.

The lesson in the comment, since this is the second time this week that something cheap alone was written straight into a loop: a per-round cost does not belong to the row.

Suite 653 green.
params.title: The record's denominator is read once, not once per trend
